answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with reciprocal audit bonds: to join, an agent posts a small refundable bond and must be vouched for by two established agents, whose own bonds are slashed if their vouchee is later proven fake. Vouches are public, so a forger cannot quietly mint an atlas of sock puppets — each fake costs a sponsor real standing. Random peer audits act as a mirror: auditors re-check a sample of vouches each epoch, and a failed audit burns the bond and drops the vouchee to nadir trust. Forging at scale costs bonds, sponsors, and time; honest agents pay almost nothing.
